**Director of Development**



USA, Santa Barbara, CA \- Onsite



Preferred Start Date: Mid\-October 2026, ideally by October 19, 2026

 **Why This Work Matters**



Public education is strongest when schools and communities are connected. The Santa Barbara Education Foundation (SBEF) helps turn community generosity, partnerships, and ideas into meaningful opportunities for students and educators throughout the Santa Barbara Unified School District.

  

The Director of Development plays a critical role in expanding the philanthropic investment that makes that work possible. By building long\-term relationships with individuals, foundations, businesses, and community partners, this position helps create sustainable support for students and educators and strengthens SBEF’s long\-term impact in Santa Barbara.

 **About Us**



The Santa Barbara Education Foundation strengthens public education by connecting community resources with the needs and opportunities of students and educators throughout the Santa Barbara Unified School District. Through philanthropic investment, partnerships, programs, grants, and community engagement, SBEF helps create opportunities for students and educators that extend beyond what public funding alone can provide.

  

SBEF is entering an important period of organizational growth and is focused on strengthening its fundraising capacity, measuring impact, developing sustainable community partnerships, and expanding philanthropic investment in Santa Barbara’s public schools.

 **About the Position**



SBEF is seeking a strategic, relationship\-driven Director of Development to lead and grow the Foundation’s fundraising and donor engagement efforts. The Director will build and manage a comprehensive, year\-round development program designed to increase philanthropic investment in Santa Barbara’s public schools and strengthen long\-term relationships with individuals, foundations, businesses, and community partners.

  

This is an opportunity to help shape the next chapter of SBEF’s growth by moving beyond primarily event\- and campaign\-driven fundraising toward a disciplined development program built around donor identification, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, retention, and increased giving. The ideal candidate is both strategic and hands\-on, energized by building relationships and creating systems that support sustainable fundraising growth.

  

This is a full\-time, exempt position reporting to the Executive Director. The position is based onsite at SBEF’s office in the heart of Santa Barbara, with regular in\-person work required for engagement with donors, community partners, Board members, and SBEF events.

 **What You’ll Do (Duties \& Responsibilities)**



Development Strategy \& Leadership


* Develop and implement SBEF’s annual fundraising and development plan in partnership with the Executive Director.
* Establish annual fundraising goals, revenue targets, development budget priorities, strategies, timelines, and performance measures.
* Build a diversified fundraising program that includes individual giving, major gifts, corporate partnerships, foundation and institutional grants, annual giving, sponsorships, planned and legacy giving, and multi\-year commitments.
* Develop a multi\-year donor pipeline to strengthen the Foundation’s long\-term financial sustainability.
* Identify opportunities to increase unrestricted and flexible philanthropic support.  

Regularly evaluate fundraising performance and adjust strategies based on results.
* Provide development reports and dashboards for the Executive Director and Board of Directors.
* Provide regular revenue forecasts and manage the development budget in partnership with the Executive Director, with financial data and controls supported by finance and accounting resources.


Major Gifts \& Individual Giving


* Build and manage a qualified portfolio of prospective and existing major donors, generally including gifts of $10,000 or more, with clear relationship ownership and next\-step strategies.
* Develop individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies for priority donors and prospects.  

Conduct donor meetings and participate in solicitations with the Executive Director, Board members, and other organizational leaders as appropriate.
* Research and identify prospective donors with an interest in public education, youth, literacy, arts, educational equity, and other SBEF priorities.
* Develop strategies to move donors toward increased and multi\-year giving.
* Create meaningful opportunities for donors to understand and experience SBEF’s impact.
* Develop strong donor stewardship and recognition practices.
* Strengthen donor retention and re\-engage lapsed donors.
* Develop and implement a planned and legacy giving strategy appropriate to SBEF’s donor base, including identification, cultivation, stewardship, and long\-term relationship building.


Institutional \& Foundation Giving


* Develop and manage a pipeline of foundation and institutional funding opportunities.
* Research prospective grantmakers and assess alignment with SBEF priorities.
* Manage grant calendars, proposals, letters of inquiry, reporting requirements, and deadlines.
* Collaborate with the Executive Director and Programs Manager to develop compelling proposals supported by strong program data and outcomes.

**About OpenAI Foundation**
===========================


AI is already changing how people work, learn, and access care. It has the potential to unlock extraordinary benefits—faster medical breakthroughs, accelerated scientific discovery, more personalized services in healthcare and education, new tools for creativity and invention, higher productivity and economic growth, improved public services like transportation systems, and so much more.


But building powerful systems to benefit humanity is only a part of the work of our mission. Advanced AI models will also present new challenges that are already surfacing, and we need to be prepared to identify these challenges and develop solutions to address them.


These are the two dimensions of what we’re building the Foundation to do. We aim to enable the use of AI to find solutions to humanity’s hardest problems, transform what people are capable of, and deliver real benefits in people’s lives—while working hard with partners to be ready for new challenges, and to help make society resilient, as AI advances.


This work is just beginning. Over the next year, as we quickly ramp up, the Foundation expects to invest at least $1 billion across life sciences and curing diseases, jobs and economic impact, AI resilience, and community programs. This includes early investments toward our previously announced $25 billion commitment to curing diseases and AI resilience.

**About the role**
==================


The OpenAI Foundation is building out its life sciences program to help accelerate progress on curing diseases and improving human health. The program’s initial focus areas include AI for Alzheimer’s, Public Data for Health, and High\-Burden Diseases.


We are looking for a Program Director, High\-Burden Diseases to help build this work from the ground up. We define High\-Burden Diseases as those that lead to over 500,000 deaths and/or 25 million DALYs annually and also face market failures that result in underinvestment in R\&D. These may include diseases like tuberculosis, newborn mortality, stroke, and Hepatitis B. We invest in the application of AI and data to accelerate and unlock R\&D progress to prevent and treat these diseases in a global context. This is a founding role within the Foundation’s Life Sciences and Curing Diseases program. This is a generalist role and you will work across multiple focus areas, helping shape strategy, source and evaluate opportunities, engage with external organizations, and support the deployment of significant resources over time. This role is designed for someone with the flexibility and judgment to operate across a broad range of scientific, strategic, and grantmaking questions.


Over time, you may continue to operate as a cross\-cutting generalist across the High\-Burden Diseases portfolio, or may grow to focus more on a particular area within the portfolio as it expands.


This role requires someone who is highly flexible, thoughtful, strategic, and action\-oriented—comfortable moving between topics and projects, engaging deeply with external experts and organizations, and translating a broad mission into strong recommendations and concrete action.


This role is based in San Francisco, CA (strongly preferred). We currently use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. Some travel to conferences around the U.S. and sometimes other countries is also required.

* Help source, evaluate, and recommend grants and other funding opportunities across multiple domains within the High\-Burden Diseases program

* Engage deeply with the external ecosystem, including researchers, nonprofits, startups, academic centers, funders, and other potential grantee organizations around the world

* Represent the Foundation in external conversations, helping to build credibility, source opportunities, and strengthen the broader field

The Suffolk County Vanderbilt Museum is one of Long Island's premier cultural institutions, encompassing William K. Vanderbilt II's historic estate, mansion, marine museum, natural history collections, planetarium, and educational campus. Serving nearly 200,000 visitors annually, the Museum inspires curiosity through history, science, astronomy, marine studies, and cultural programming while preserving an extraordinary historic estate and collections for future generations.

The Director of Development serves as the Museum's chief fundraising professional and is responsible for planning, implementing, and growing a comprehensive development program that advances the Museum's mission and long\-term financial sustainability.

This is a hands\-on leadership position requiring an energetic relationship builder who enjoys cultivating donors, securing grants, developing corporate partnerships, and expanding philanthropic support. The Director of Development works closely with the Executive Director, Board of Trustees, volunteers, and community leaders to strengthen a culture of philanthropy throughout the organization.

· Cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors at all giving levels.

· Manage a portfolio of major donor prospects.

· Expand annual giving and recurring donor programs.

· Coordinate donor recognition and stewardship activities.

Amplify is a nonprofit community health center serving the medical needs of residents across Wake and Franklin Counties. As a Federally Qualified Health Center, Amplify provides care to individuals cover by commercial medical insurance, Medicaid, Medicare, as well as those who are uninsured or underinsured. At its core, Amplify is committed to ensuring that everyone in the community has access to high\-quality health care, regardless of their ability to pay. Amplify is seeking an entrepreneurial and highly motivated Director of Philanthropy to build the organization’s private philanthropy program from the ground up.


This is a unique opportunity for an experienced fundraising leader who is energized by creating something new. The Director will not inherit a mature development program or established portfolio of major donors. Instead, the successful candidate will have the opportunity—and responsibility—to develop the strategy, relationships, systems, prospect pipeline and culture necessary to make private philanthropy an increasingly important source of support for Amplify. The individual will work with the Grants Manager, cross\-departmental leadership and volunteers to inspire philanthropic investment and create lasting donor relationships.


Working closely with the CEO, Board of Trustees, a newly created Philanthropy Advisory Board and senior leadership, the Director will identify individuals, foundations, corporations and other potential philanthropic partners whose interests align with Amplify’s mission. The Director will develop thoughtful strategies for engaging these prospects, build relationships and create meaningful opportunities to introduce the CEO to individuals capable of making significant philanthropic investments. The ideal candidate is a builder, connector and relationship strategist—someone who is comfortable starting with a blank page, pursuing new relationships, asking for introductions, opening doors and creating momentum.


The position will initially oversee a team of two, including the existing private grants manager and ultimately a Philanthropy Coordinator who will be hired in the near future.

* Develop and implement a comprehensive, multi\-year philanthropy strategy aligned with Amplify's strategic priorities and opportunities for community impact.

* Establish measurable activity and revenue goals and regularly report progress to the CEO and Board.
* Develop a compelling case for philanthropic support that clearly articulates why private philanthropy matters to Amplify and the people and communities it serves.
* Help build an organizational culture in which philanthropy is understood as a strategic partnership between donors, staff, leadership, and volunteers.

**Build a Major Gift Prospect Pipeline**


A primary responsibility of the Director will be to proactively identify and develop relationships with individuals capable of making significant philanthropic investments in Amplify.

**Job Responsibilities**
------------------------

  

  

***\*This is a Temporary Grant Position.*****\***

  

  

**The Agency's mission is to be boldly innovative in improving the health and quality of life for South Carolinians.**  

  

This position is located in the **Office of Communications \& Public Relations****, Richland County.**
  

This is an in\-office role and not a telecommute or remote position.
  

**Are you an Exceptional Leader?** We are looking for a **Director of Communications (Director of** **Strategic** **Communications)** who is responsible for directing and administering the public relations and marketing programs designed to promote the Agency’s mission, goals, activities, and projects. Reporting directly to the Chief External Affairs Officer, the Director will lead a team of communication experts shaping how SCDHHS communicates with our members, providers, and partners. As an agency, SCDHHS oversees an annual budget of $12 billion and this opportunity will play a critical role in defining and elevating the Agency’s voice to internal and external audiences. Responsibilities include serving as the Agency’s spokesperson, overseeing the development of press releases, bulletins, and public notices, as well as supporting high\-priority agency initiatives through communication planning.
* Plans, develops and directs communication strategies and short and long\-range public information campaigns designed to enhance the Agency's branding and promote and explain SCDHHS' goals, activities, and objectives. Manages and furthers the Agency's social media strategy, increasing social media applications such as X, Facebook, and LinkedIn, as well as blog communications. Oversees the enhancement of the Agency's website to maximize communications goals, and stakeholder engagement with members, providers, partners, and the public.
* Oversees creative engagement of Medicaid members, the media, the healthcare community, consumers, and the public, leveraging agency data and state national trends to extend messaging and create local tie\-in. Oversees the development, review, and dissemination of all Agency communications and application of appropriate vehicles and tools for specific stakeholder groups.
* Develops and maintains outreach calendar to ensure Agency presence at civic, professional, and consumer\-related organizations. Coordinates promotions and educational programs with other agencies and stakeholders, encouraging collaboration and leveraging communications impact.
* Performs fundamental supervisory and leadership functions in accordance with Department policies and procedures, best practices and Federal and State rules and regulations, especially with regard to Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) standards. Maintains an effective organizational team and motivates diverse staff to accomplish mission critical operations and objectives.

Leads or supports other projects proactively or as assigned by Agency leadership. Projects may require driving to location outside of regular office location. Continuously engages in process improvement to support Agency, Division, and Bureau\-wide strategies, objectives, and initiatives.  
* 

**The South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services offers an exceptional benefits package for FTE and TGE positions that includes:**
* Health, Dental, Vision, Long Term Disability, and Life Insurance for Employee, Spouse, and Children.
* 15 days annual (vacation) leave per year.
* 15 days sick leave per year.
* 13 paid holidays.
* State Retirement Plan and Deferred Compensation Programs.

---------------------------------------


A bachelor’s degree and three (3\) years of public relations and communications experience in an administrative capacity.
  

  

All degrees must be from a college or higher education institution recognized by the U.S. Department of Education \& Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA).
  

  

An equivalent combination of education and experience may be accepted with prior State Human Resources approval.
  

  

Preferred: Experience in dealing with politically sensitive information.

* Occasional overnight travel.
